routes.label: Estimate from a nearby tripling date

question:
Problems \(15,\) \(16,\) and \(17\) all refer to the following:

Don’t Crowd The Isles

In the very center of the Irenic Sea lie the beautiful Nisos Isles. In \(1998\) the number of people on these islands is only \(200,\) but the population triples every \(25\) years. Queen Irene has decreed that there must be at least \(1.5\) square miles for every person living in the Isles. The total area of the Nisos Isles is \(24{,}900\) square miles.

Estimate the population of Nisos in the year \(2050.\)
solution:
For the intended rough estimate, assume growth is spread reasonably steadily through each \(25\)-year period, so that two additional years make only a modest difference.

From \(1998\) to \(2050\) is \(52\) years, close to two \(25\)-year periods. After those two periods, in \(2048\), the population is
\[
200\times3\times3=1800.
\]
Thus about \(2000\) people, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\), is the intended estimate.

The statement does not specify that within-period assumption. For example, suppose that in every \(25\)-year period the population increases by \(50\%\) after two years and doubles at the end. Each period still multiplies the population by \(1.5\times2=3\). This schedule gives \(1800\) people in \(2048\), followed by \(2700\) in \(2050\), which is closest to \(3000\), choice E. Consequently, D is conditional on the intended growth interpretation, rather than forced by the stated rule alone.
